Empirical Research Plan  
“Total costs to firms that misrepresent their financial statements”

=====================================================================
1. Identification Strategy
=====================================================================
Main strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with staggered treatment timing, supplemented by a short-window event-study for the initial stock-price response.

Why DID?  
• Costs materialise after the revelation of misconduct. 585 firms are “treated” at different calendar dates (1978–2002).  
• A matched sample of non-target firms provides a plausible counterfactual path for stock-market and real outcomes had the AAER firms not been caught.  
• The approach can capture medium- and long-run outcomes (e.g., three-year abnormal return, changes in leverage, asset growth, lawsuit payments) that the narrow event-study window cannot.  
• We can implement modern staggered-adoption DID estimators (Callaway-Sant’Anna, Gardner-Sun) that remain valid when treatment timing differs.

Short-window event study: measures the immediate market-value loss on two focal dates (misconduct revelation and final SEC order) to benchmark against longer-run DID estimates.

=====================================================================
2. Treatment and Control
=====================================================================
Treatment variable  
TREAT_i = 1 for firm i that appears in an AAER for financial misrepresentation; 0 otherwise.

Treatment timing  
Event date τ_i = first public announcement of the misconduct (earlier of restatement or SEC investigation press release). Day 0 of event study; year 0 for DID.

Control group  
One‐to-one (or 1:3) nearest-neighbour match on:  
• 2-digit SIC,  
• log(total assets),  
• fiscal year,  
and NOT mentioned in any AAER in the sample window.

Observation window  
t = −5,…,+5 fiscal years around τ_i. We drop firms that subsequently become treated to avoid “never-treated” contamination (or use CS estimator that re-weights them).

No RDD: no running variable / cutoff relevant.

=====================================================================
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
=====================================================================
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of enforcement, outcomes for target and matched control firms would have evolved similarly.  
• Plausibility: Matching on industry and size mitigates differential trends; we will test pre-trends graphically and with leads of treatment.

A2. No spillovers / interference: The shock to Firm i does not directly affect matched controls.  
• Plausibility: Except for direct competitors, contagion should be limited; we can drop closest product-market rivals (e.g., same 4-digit SIC) as robustness.

A3. No anticipatory effects: Investors and regulators learn about misconduct only at τ_i.  
• Plausibility: Some leakages possible; we will run placebo event windows (−40, −10) to test for pre-announcement price drift.

A4. Stable unit composition: Treated and control firms remain in the panel post-event (no differential delisting).  
• We will track delistings; apply inverse-probability weights or Lee bounds if attrition differs.

=====================================================================
4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
=====================================================================
T1. Endogenous match quality / hidden differences  
• Use entropy balancing and many-to-one matching to equalise pre-event means.  
• Include firm and year FE; control for ROA, leverage, MB, and stock liquidity.

T2. Anticipation or gradual information leakage  
• Examine cumulative abnormal returns (CARs) in multiple pre-event windows (−180, −20).  
• Shift treatment date earlier if leakages are systematic (e.g., first newspaper rumour).

T3. Concurrent shocks (industry scandals, macro events)  
• Include industry-year fixed effects.  
• Cluster SEs at the firm and calendar-year levels.  
• Run leave-one-industry-out analyses to ensure results are not driven by a single scandal wave (e.g., 2001–02 telecoms).

=====================================================================
5. R Code Outline
=====================================================================
```r
#--- 0. Packages -----------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)       # DID regressions
library(ExPost)       # Callaway-Sant’Anna DID
library(EventStudy)   # abnormal return calculation
library(MatchIt)      # matching
setDTthreads(8)

#--- 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------
aaer   <- fread("AAER_master.csv")          # one row per enforcement
crsp   <- fread("CRSP_daily.csv")           # daily returns
comp   <- fread("Compustat_annual.csv")     # accounting vars
pen    <- fread("Penalties.csv")            # fines, settlements

#--- 2. Construct treatment panel -----------------------------------
# Keep first announcement date
aaer[, event_date := as.IDate(first_public_date)]
aaer[, TREAT := 1L]

# Match controls (nearest neighbour on SIC2, log assets, fiscal year)
match_data <- merge(aaer[, .(gvkey, fyear, sic2, lassets = log(at))],
                    comp[, .(gvkey, fyear, sic2 = substr(sic,1,2),
                             lassets=log(at))],
                    by=c("gvkey","fyear","sic2","lassets"), all.y=TRUE)

m.out <- matchit(TREAT ~ lassets, data = match_data,
                 method = "nearest", ratio = 3)
controls <- data.table(match.data(m.out))[TREAT==0, unique(gvkey)]

#--- 3. Event-study CARs --------------------------------------------
# Abnormal return over (-1,+1) window around event_date
estudy <- eventstudy(stock_data = crsp,
                     event_list = aaer[,.(permno,event_date)],
                     estimation_window = c(-250,-30),
                     event_window = c(-1,1),
                     market_model = "market")

#--- 4. Build DID panel (-5 … +5 fiscal years) ----------------------
panel <- merge(comp, aaer[,.(gvkey, event_fyear=fyear, TREAT)], by="gvkey", all.x=TRUE)
panel[, rel_year := fyear - event_fyear]        # -5 … +5
panel <- panel[rel_year %between% c(-5,5)]

# Identify never-treated controls
panel[, ever_treated := max(TREAT, na.rm=TRUE), by=gvkey]
panel[, treat_year := ifelse(TREAT==1, rel_year, NA)]
panel[, G := fifelse(ever_treated==1, event_fyear, 0)]  # 0 = never

#--- 5. Main DID (Callaway-Sant’Anna) -------------------------------
cs_res <- att_gt(yname   = "car_0_1",     # or ROA, leverage...
                 gname   = "G",
                 idname  = "gvkey",
                 tname   = "fyear",
                 xformla = ~ log(at) + mb + leverage,
                 data    = panel,
                 allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE,
                 est_method = "dr")

agg_effect <- aggte(cs_res, type="group")  # overall ATT

#--- 6. Robustness: placebo pre-event treatment ---------------------
panel_placebo <- panel[rel_year<=-2]  # leads only
placebo <- feols(car_0_1 ~ i(rel_year, TREAT, ref=-1) |
                   gvkey + fyear, data = panel_placebo,
                 cluster = "gvkey")
etable(placebo, se="cluster")
```

=====================================================================
6. Expected Results
=====================================================================
• Immediate market-value loss (CAR −1/+1) on the first public announcement: −8 % to −12 % (median firm).  
• Additional −3 % to −5 % around the final SEC order.  
• Three-year buy-and-hold abnormal return: −25 % relative to matched controls.  
• Direct cash penalties average 1 %–2 % of pre-event market capitalisation; reputational loss (long-run equity decline) an order of magnitude larger.

Direction: negative; magnitude large because revelation destroys intangible trust capital and raises cost of capital.

=====================================================================
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment
(1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)
=====================================================================
C1. No differential pre-trends……………… 0.8  
C2. No anticipation…………………………… 0.7  
C3. No spillovers/interference…………… 0.8  
C4. Stable sample / limited attrition…… 0.6  
C5. Correct inference for staggered DID… 0.9  

Overall: 3.8/5 – credible but requires careful pre-trend and attrition checks.
